newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM Banharn to dissolve parliament - deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM Banharn to dissolve parliament - deputy PM.

text.p: Thailand's outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa will dissolve parlaiment and call a snap election on November 17, deputy prime minister Samak Sundaravej said on Friday.

Banharn had decided to dissolve the house because there was no full agreement reached among members of his six-party coalition on the choice of a new prime minister to succeed him, Samak told reporters. He added Banharn would make an announcement later.
Banharn, who was forced by his allies to quit within seven days last Saturday, had kept the nation and his coalition allies in the dark for six days over who his choice of succesor would be.
"There was a deadlock on the choice (of a new prime minister)," Samak said after a meeting of the coalition's leaders with Banharn.

Many coalition sources had expected Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh to be nominated by Banharn as he appeard to have strong support. But manouvering by Chavalit to gain support failed when key members of Banharn's core Chart Thai party refused to support him, coalition sources said.
A royal proclamation on holding a fresh election is expected later, government sources said.
